title: Initial scaffold: trigger logic + poller
body:
## Summary

First slice of the self-hosted PR review agent from #1: the **trigger
pipeline** and the **outbound-only GitHub poller**. Nothing here spends
tokens or posts to GitHub — the spending rails land before anything can
spend, per the phase ordering in #1.

25 files, +1836. Two commits: the initial scaffold, and a follow-up
addressing the first review round (rate-limit hardening, decision logging).

## What's in

### Trigger classifier — `src/pr_review_agent/triggers/`

Exactly two events start a review:

1. a freshly opened PR whose **author** is allowlisted;
2. a comment containing `@claude` whose **commenter** is allowlisted.

Gating the mention on the commenter is what lets a maintainer summon a
review of an outside contribution that would not be auto-reviewed.

| Rejected event | Reason code |
| :-- | :-- |
| Push to an existing PR | never classified — the poller emits no push event |
| Draft PR | `draft` |
| PR from an unlisted author | `author_not_allowlisted` |
| Comment from an unlisted account | `commenter_not_allowlisted` |
| Any bot, including the agent itself | `bot_author` / `bot_commenter` |
| `@claude` in a fence, code span or blockquote | `no_mention` |
| Already-open PR seen on first poll | `not_fresh` |

Two decisions worth knowing:

- **Allowlisting is on the numeric user id, never the login.** A login can
  be renamed and the freed name registered by somebody else. A login in
  `config.yaml` raises at startup rather than never matching.
- **The cold-start watermark is load-bearing.** The poller sees *open* PRs,
  not `opened` events; without it the first poll would review the whole
  backlog in one pass.

Every accept/reject decision is logged with its reason code.

### Config loader — `src/pr_review_agent/config.py`

Strict `config.yaml` loader. Unknown keys and malformed values raise
`ConfigError` at startup; a typo in a safety setting must never fall back
to a default that spends tokens. `config.example.yaml` is shipped and
tested as loadable.

### Poller — `src/pr_review_agent/poller/`

- Three **repo-wide** endpoints per cycle (`/pulls?state=open`,
  `/issues/comments`, `/pulls/comments`) — one request per endpoint
  regardless of how many PRs are open, which is what keeps the rate-limit
  arithmetic in #1 true.
- **ETag conditional GETs.** A `304` costs nothing against the rate limit.
- **Adaptive interval:** 10 s while active, ×2 decay per quiet cycle to a
  600 s ceiling, snapping back to the floor on any `200`.
- **Rate-limit handling:** bounded retries on `403`/`429` carrying
  `Retry-After` (a plain `403` — bad token — is not retried), transport
  errors wrapped in `GitHubClientError`, malformed headers tolerated, and
  the interval forced to its ceiling when `x-ratelimit-remaining` reaches
  the configured floor.

### Dedupe keys

    pr_opened:{repo}:{pr}:{head_sha}
    mention:{repo}:{pr}:{comment_id}

The mention key excludes `head_sha` on purpose: the same comment must never
trigger twice, and a later push must not revive it.

## Not in this PR

Deliberately deferred, in dependency order:

- Mapping poll payloads to `PullRequest` / `Comment` and feeding the
  classifier; the loop that calls `poll_once()` on a schedule
- Queue and per-PR lease (SQLite)
- Budget governor — **lands before the review worker**
- `ReviewEngine` adapter, publisher, retention sweep
- GitHub token plumbing and the reviewer account id

## Follow-ups

- #3 — persist the watermark and ETag cache; decide how `/issues/comments`
  payloads map to a PR (`head_sha`, `pr_number`, plain-issue filter, draft
  vs. mention); migrate `GitHubClient` to async.
- #4 — PR-Agent as a second `ReviewEngine` (`pr_agent_litellm`), API-key
  mode only.

## Verification

    python -m pytest -q          # 122 passed, no network, no tokens
    python -m ruff check .       # clean
    python -m ruff format --check .

The trigger pipeline is pure functions over fixtures; the poller tests use
`httpx.MockTransport`.

Refs #1

title: Adopt DTaaS CLI project conventions: Poetry, CI workflow, agent guidelines
body:
## Summary

Restructures the project along the lines of the `cli` package in
[INTO-CPS-Association/DTaaS](https://github.com/INTO-CPS-Association/DTaaS), so
the two repositories are set up, checked and built the same way.

## Packaging

- Move from setuptools + `pip install -e ".[dev]"` to **Poetry**, with the
  dependency set locked in a committed `poetry.lock`.
- Metadata stays in the `[tool.poetry]` form rather than PEP 621's `[project]`
  table. This is deliberate: Poetry 1.8 (still shipped by several
  distributions, and what is installed on this machine) cannot read `[project]`
  metadata at all and refuses to run, whereas Poetry 2.x reads
  `[tool.poetry]` with deprecation warnings only. Install, lock, test and build
  were verified end to end under **both 1.8.2 and 2.4.3**.
- `poetry.toml` pins the virtualenv to `./.venv`, so local runs and CI agree on
  one interpreter.

## Quality gates

- Add **pylint** (the shared `.pylintrc` from DTaaS) and **pyright** alongside
  the existing ruff configuration, plus **pytest-cov**.
- Add the docstrings pylint was missing on `src`, taking it from 9.65 to
  **10.00/10**.
- Fix the one pyright error: `_send_with_retries` passed a possibly-`None`
  `Retry-After` header into `_parse_retry_after(value: str)`. The retry
  condition is restructured so the `None` case returns early and narrows the
  type. Behaviour is unchanged and the poller tests still pass.
- `.pylintrc` gains an `init-hook` putting `src` on `sys.path`, so pylint
  resolves the package under this src layout without depending on an install.

## CI

Adds a single `.github/workflows/python-ci.yml`, flattening the split DTaaS
uses (`python-cli.yml` + `python-reusable.yml`) since this repository holds one
package:

- `test` — Ubuntu, macOS and Windows. Installs Poetry with `pipx`, runs
  `poetry install --with dev`, then pytest with coverage. Formatting, ruff,
  pylint (`src` and `tests`), pyright and the coverage artefact run on Ubuntu
  only, to avoid paying three times for a platform-independent result.
- `build` — verifies the lock file matches `pyproject.toml`, installs with
  `--only main`, builds the wheel and sdist, rejects direct-URL
  (`file://`, `git+`, `https://`) dependencies in the built metadata, and
  uploads the artefacts.

Every CI step is a `poetry run ...` command that can be run locally, so a CI
failure is always reproducible on a laptop.

## Documentation

- `CLAUDE.md` — behavioural guidelines adapted from the DTaaS original, plus a
  project-specific section on spending, identity/trust and verification.
- `AGENTS.md` — coding-assistant conventions and the project layout.
- `DEVELOPER.md` — dependencies, code structure, setup, testing, linting, type
  checking, building and CI.
- README's Development section now gives the Poetry commands; it previously
  gave Windows-only `venv/Scripts/python.exe` paths.

## Verification

Run locally from a clean `.venv`, every step exiting 0 (`set -e`):

```
pytest         122 passed, 98% coverage
ruff format    21 files already formatted
ruff check     All checks passed!
pylint src     10.00/10
pylint tests    9.28/10  (>= 9.0 gate)
pyright        0 errors, 0 warnings
poetry check --lock / poetry build   wheel + sdist built, no direct-URL deps
```

title: Close PR #2 follow-ups (#5), land the deferred poller infrastructure (#3), and restructure the docs
body:
Closes #3. Closes #5. Moves the system design from #1 into `docs/`.

## Issue #5 — small follow-ups

| Change | Where |
| :-- | :-- |
| `_coerce_user_id` parses and validates in one step, so `"--5"` can no longer pass a shape check and then raise a bare `ValueError` out of the config loader. Non-positive ids rejected. | `triggers/allowlist.py` |
| Cap an honoured `Retry-After` at 60 s; parse the RFC 9110 HTTP-date form as a deadline instead of mapping it to 1 s. A longer cooldown is returned un-retried for the poller to schedule. Primary-limit behaviour documented. A non-JSON `200` body is wrapped in `GitHubClientError`. | `poller/client.py` |
| Operator-relevant rejections log at `INFO`; only `not_fresh` and `no_mention`, which fire on every poll, stay at `DEBUG`. The agent's own events report `self_author`/`self_commenter` rather than `bot_*`. | `triggers/classifier.py` |
| `per_page=100` on all three paths, with the sort-order invariant the design rests on written down. | `poller/endpoints.py` |
| A naive `since` is rejected at construction rather than `TypeError`-ing on the first pull request seen. | `triggers/classifier.py` |
| `Actor.from_api` raises a typed `PayloadError` on a ghost (`"user": null`) account. | `triggers/models.py` |
| `bash*` back to `bash/`. | `.gitignore` |

A CI workflow and the notifications-API note were the two remaining §5 items; the workflow already landed in #6, and the note is now in `docs/POLLER.md`.

**Left undone, deliberately:** `strip_non_prose` normalising CRLF and dropping a trailing newline. It is cosmetic for its only caller, and changing it adds risk without benefit. It is recorded under "Known gaps" in `docs/ROADMAP.md` so it is not rediscovered as a bug.

## Issue #3 — the three deferred infrastructure items

**1. Persistence.** `store.py` adds a WAL-mode SQLite watermark and ETag store. Watermarks are namespaced per stream and **only ever move forward**, so a restart or an out-of-order settle cannot walk one backwards and replay an old `@claude` — which is spent allowance, not a wasted poll. `SqliteStore` satisfies a new `ETagCache` protocol, so it drops straight into `Poller` where the in-memory `ETagStore` goes.

**2. Comment payload mapping.** `poller/payloads.py` maps raw REST payloads to trigger models, and resolves the three quirks that forced the design:

- the pull request number comes from `issue_url` / `pull_request_url`, so it costs no extra request;
- plain issue comments are filtered on `html_url` containing `/pull/`, so `@claude` in issue #7 does not start a review;
- `head_sha` is **left for claim time**. Resolving it at poll time would cost one request per comment per cycle to learn a value that can go stale before the worker starts, and the worker already re-reads it before posting. `Comment.head_sha` and `Trigger.head_sha` are therefore `str | None`; the mention dedupe key never included it.

The draft question: **the draft rule does not apply to mentions.** `draft` exists to stop unasked-for auto-review; an allowlisted human typing `@claude` on a draft is the ask.

An unmappable item is skipped with a warning rather than failing the cycle — one malformed item must not stop the other ninety-nine.

**3. Async client.** `GitHubClient` and `Poller` are now asyncio-native. The daemon is specified as asyncio and the queue, leases and governor will be built on this; a synchronous `get` would block the loop through a rate-limit backoff. Done now because it touches every poller test through `MockTransport`, and would only get more expensive. Adds `pytest-asyncio` with `asyncio_mode = "auto"`.

## Documentation

`README.md` is now product-facing — the one rule, what starts a review, how it polls, status, quickstart, and a routing table. `DEVELOPER.md` keeps only the toolchain. `docs/` carries the detail, including the system design from #1:

| Document | Covers |
| :-- | :-- |
| `docs/DESIGN.md` | The four constraints, every alternative considered and rejected, repository placement, generalisation to other agents, the open billing-mode question, prompt injection, retention |
| `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | The seven components, the path an event takes, package layout, layering, the 3.10 shim |
| `docs/TRIGGERS.md` | Every reason code and its log level, what counts as a mention, dedupe keys, why identity is a number |
| `docs/POLLER.md` | The three endpoints, rate-limit arithmetic, adaptive interval, retry rules, payload mapping, why not the notifications API |
| `docs/STORAGE.md` | Why SQLite, what a lost watermark costs, the schema |
| `docs/BUDGET.md` | Specification only: five layers, reserve-then-settle, degradation ladder, self-calibrating breaker |
| `docs/CONFIG.md` | Every key, and why unknown keys are an error |
| `docs/ROADMAP.md` | What is built, what is next, the acceptance checklist, known gaps |

## Spending

**No change widens what triggers a review or removes a cap.** The one behavioural change to trigger scope is a narrowing: plain issue comments, previously unfiltered because nothing mapped payloads at all, are now dropped before the classifier sees them. The suite stays pure functions over fixtures plus `MockTransport` and `tmp_path` — no network, no tokens.

## Verification

```
171 passed, 98% coverage
ruff format --check: 50 files already formatted
ruff check: All checks passed!
pylint src: 10.00/10   pylint tests: 9.32/10
pyright: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations
poetry check --lock: All set!
poetry build: wheel + sdist built
```
